text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Foreign minister Stoyan Stalev left for Brussels for talks on Bulgaria's integration in the European Union. Stalev is also expected to discuss aid to secure grain imports and balance of payments support for Bulgaria.
-- Bank of England is expected to advise Bulgaria on the sale of the country's foreign trade companies, Trade ministry officials said. @
-- Bulgaria's trade turnover with Greece was $660 million in 1996, deputy Trade minister Minko Gerdzhikov said.

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet should consider selling up to 100 percent of the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company (BTC) and not just 25 percent as initially planned if that would bring an optimal price, World Bank Southeastern Department director Kenneth Lay said.

-- Defectors from Bulgaria's former ruling Socialist party set up an Euro-Left political movement and elected Alexander Tomov, who came forth in the presidential elections last year, as a leader of the new formation.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet is expected to liberalise prices of basic goods, including bread, meat, milk and transport, prime minister Stefan Sofianski said.
-- The World Bank may extend some $200 million to support Bulgaria's structural reforms, Word Bank Southeastern Department director Kenneth Lay, said. @

-- Bulgaria may start negotiations to reshedule the country's debt to the government creditors of the Paris Club amounting to $1.4 billion once an agreement with the International Monetary Fund is signed, central bank officials said.
-- Bulgaria's interim government is expected to discuss raising wages in the public sector by 55 percent to update incomes with rising prices, Labour and social care minister Ivan Neikov said.
